title: Greenwich LifeSciences is still climbing a day after a 36% jump — onconference abstracts, not new trial data. Momentum, or a setup fordisappointment?
author: tickeron_community
selftext:
\[GLSI\]([https://tickeron.com/ticker/GLSI/](https://tickeron.com/ticker/GLSI/)) jumped 12.19% in  
regular-session trading today, from Tuesday's close of $18.70 to  
$20.98 by late morning, extending the prior session's roughly +36%  
surge (from $13.76 to $18.72).  
  
The catalyst was Tuesday's company release, not a new one today: two  
FLAMINGO-01 Phase III abstracts were accepted for poster presentation  
at the San Antonio Breast Cancer Symposium on December 9. The release  
carried no new trial data. Today's extension has no fresh company  
disclosure and is consistent with momentum and short covering, with  
roughly 20% of the small float held short.  
  
The write-up on today's follow-through, and what was (and wasn't) in  
the abstract news:  
[https://tickeron.com/blogs/why-is-greenwich-lifesciences-glsi-stock-up-12-19-today-40395/](https://tickeron.com/blogs/why-is-greenwich-lifesciences-glsi-stock-up-12-19-today-40395/)  
  
How much of a +50% two-day move can abstract acceptances really  
support if the data itself hasn't changed?  
  
Not financial advice. Figures are from today's midday write-up, not a  
live quote.

comments.author: Odd_Project9696
comments.body: Maybe is in correlation with other companies that have succeeded with their trials.  SLS, Moderna. I would like some opinions on this. Should we consider for long?
